prompt:

Preserve the user's requested identities, counts, setting, and layout. Add no default motifs.
VISUAL MEDIUM: oil_painting_with_compressed_color_planes
REPRESENTATION: stylized
APPLY THESE AUTHORED VISUAL RULES:
- [performer-color-masses] Reduce each requested performer to no more than four broad opaque color masses. Give each body a distinct dominant angle or height; omit facial features, garment seams, and small anatomy unless the user requests them, so the performer remains readable through silhouette, instrument, and gesture rather than illustration detail.
- [alternating-performance-rhythm] Alternate upright and oblique blocks across the requested action; vary their scale and intervals so the scene has a readable pulse without imposing a fixed left-to-right order.
- [selective-action-cues] Use only a few narrow contrasting marks to indicate instrument direction and the main arm gesture; leave faces, hands, and clothing largely unmodeled so the larger color masses stay dominant.
- [movement-in-painted-masses] Keep each requested performer countable, use alternating weighted planes to carry the motion, and reserve narrow marks for the instruments or gestures that identify the action.

scope.description: An optional direction for a user-requested dance or music performance. Preserve the requested performer count and action, but translate bodies, instruments, and the stage into a few broad, weighted color masses. Vary vertical and diagonal blocks to carry rhythm; use only a few narrow edges or gaps to keep gestures and instruments distinguishable. It does not prescribe a café, stadium, specific dance, instrument, or named composition.
limitations: Activate only when the user requests a dance or music performance scene.
Preserve requested performer count, identities, instruments, choreography, and setting.
Make figures recognizable through pose and color-plane relationship, not anatomical detail.
Do not add a café, stage, audience, sports field, or instrument unless it appears in the user's request.
Do not reproduce a named painting or its figure arrangement.

rules.applies_when: The user requests one or more performers in a dance or music scene.
rules.instruction: Reduce each requested performer to no more than four broad opaque color masses. Give each body a distinct dominant angle or height; omit facial features, garment seams, and small anatomy unless the user requests them, so the performer remains readable through silhouette, instrument, and gesture rather than illustration detail.
rules.observable: Performer count and action remain readable from silhouettes, distinct block angles, instruments, and a few gesture cues; each figure visibly uses a small number of large color masses.
rules.reject_when: Bodies merge into one undifferentiated block, the requested count changes, or faces, garment folds, and anatomy details dominate instead of a few broad color masses.
rules.avoid: polished portraits, uniform body shapes, and copied figure placement

rules.applies_when: The user requests multiple performers or a visible movement phrase.
rules.instruction: Alternate upright and oblique blocks across the requested action; vary their scale and intervals so the scene has a readable pulse without imposing a fixed left-to-right order.
rules.observable: The eye can follow the movement across distinct masses while open gaps prevent a crowded, continuous silhouette.
rules.reject_when: All figures repeat one static pose, the user-requested choreography changes, or unrelated diagonal shapes dominate the action.
rules.avoid: decorative zigzags, unrequested audience rows, and copied composition

rules.applies_when: The scene includes instruments, held props, or identifiable dance gestures.
rules.instruction: Use only a few narrow contrasting marks to indicate instrument direction and the main arm gesture; leave faces, hands, and clothing largely unmodeled so the larger color masses stay dominant.
rules.observable: Requested instruments and the main action remain identifiable, while each performer still reads first as a handful of weighted paint planes rather than a detailed illustration.
rules.reject_when: Instrument or limb cues disappear, or outlines and small details cover most color fields.
rules.avoid: detailed musical notation, readable text, and thin uniform outlining

joint_checks.instruction: Keep each requested performer countable, use alternating weighted planes to carry the motion, and reserve narrow marks for the instruments or gestures that identify the action.
joint_checks.observable: The scene reads as the requested performance through silhouettes, angle, and a small number of action cues while thick color masses remain dominant.
